levels.title: Check Your Edge Cases First
levels.body_md: Look closely at how your program handles the smallest weights. Does your check give the right answer for the smallest even weight?
levels.question_back: Does your check give the right answer for the smallest even weight?

levels.title: Sum Of Two Positive Evens
levels.body_md: Think about what numbers can be written as a sum of two positive even numbers. Why must such a total be even and larger than two.

levels.title: Your Condition Is Correct
levels.body_md: Your test in `w % 2 == 0 && w > 2` on `L6` covers this perfectly. Odd weights fail the first part, and weight two fails the second part, so no failing input exists.

levels.title: Why Your Logic Works
levels.body_md: Any split needs `w = a + b` with `a` and `b` both positive and even. The smallest such sum is `2 + 2 = 4`, so `w` must be even and greater than `2`. Your `L6` checks exactly that, so `8` gives `YES` and `1`, `2`, `3` give `NO` correctly. No change is needed to your lines. This is `O(1)` time and `O(1)` memory.
